results.corrected_title: Microsoft unveils Maia 300 inference chip at OCP Global Summit, targets gigawatt-scale deployment from 2027
results.corrected_summary: On 12 October 2026, at the OCP Global Summit in San Jose, Microsoft unveiled the Maia 300, its third-generation in-house AI inference accelerator. Each chip has 288GB of HBM4 at 18 TB/s, a 950W power budget and compute chiplets made on TSMC's N2P process. Microsoft says it delivers 40% more tokens per megawatt than 'leading GPU-based systems', but it did not name the systems it compared against. Microsoft plans to scale Maia to gigawatt levels and make it the main inference platform for its own products from 2027. Reuters reported that more than 1 million chips could be deployed next year, but Microsoft has not confirmed that figure.
key_facts: Unveiled 12 Oct 2026 at OCP Global Summit, San Jose
288GB HBM4 (8 stacks), 18 TB/s, 950W, TSMC N2P compute chiplets
96-chip rack draws about 167 kW and gives up to 7x the token throughput of a Maia 200 rack (Microsoft claim)
Claims 40% more tokens per megawatt than unnamed leading GPU systems
Gigawatt-scale rollout planned; main Microsoft inference system from 2027
results.issues: The Redmond Magazine URL returned 403, so the claims were confirmed through other outlets. The candidate's 'several GW from 2027' is phrased as 'gigawatt scale' in the coverage. No source I found gave a specific multi-GW figure, so that number was dropped. The 40% claim is Microsoft's own and uses an unnamed baseline. The candidate's why_it_matters line (analysts blaming the chip for this week's chip-stock fall) was not verified.

results.corrected_title: Ramp valued at $60bn after $1.85bn funding round
results.corrected_summary: Corporate card and finance software company Ramp has raised $1.85bn at a $60bn valuation, up from $44bn in a $750m round in June 2026. Dragoneer, Thrive Capital, Founders Fund, Sands Capital and Avenir Growth co-led the round. Ramp says annualised revenue has passed $2bn and it now has 85,000 customers. It is building AI agents into procurement, expense management, accounting and budgeting.
key_facts: Co-led by Dragoneer, Thrive Capital, Founders Fund, Sands Capital and Avenir Growth
Valued at $44bn in a $750m round in June 2026
Annualised revenue above $2bn (from $1.5bn in June); 85,000 customers (from 70,000)
Annualised purchase volume above $275bn, up 175% year on year
results.issues: The candidate says the round was 'led by Dragoneer and Thrive'. In fact it was co-led by five firms. The FinTech Futures source was not opened.

results.corrected_title: Taiwan plans $2-4bn US industrial parks for AI hardware suppliers, starting in Texas
results.corrected_summary: Taiwan's Economy Minister Kung Ming-hsin told Bloomberg that the government supports building industrial parks in the US, starting in Texas. The parks would help smaller suppliers to TSMC and AI server makers such as Foxconn set up US operations. Each park is estimated to cost $2-4bn. Private businesses would provide the money, working with the Taiwan Electrical and Electronic Manufacturers' Association (TEEMA), while the government offers loan guarantees and help with visas and land. The economy ministry said it would give details on the Texas land later.
key_facts: Minister Kung Ming-hsin made the remarks to Bloomberg; the MOEA commented on 16 Oct 2026 (Taipei time)
Texas is the first of more than one planned US site
Privately funded with TEEMA; government provides loan guarantees, visa and land help
Aimed at smaller suppliers to TSMC and AI server makers such as Foxconn (Bloomberg also named Nvidia)
results.issues: Neither opened source links the parks to the US-Taiwan trade deal or mentions the $250bn credit guarantees. The $250bn guarantee commitment comes from the earlier trade deal and is not part of this announcement, so it was removed. Reports put the date as either 15 or 16 Oct, probably because of the time zone of the Bloomberg report; both dates fall inside the window. Bloomberg reported that land in Texas was already secured; the MOEA neither confirmed nor denied this.
